# Incident Report: Koi Stealer Infection — DESKTOP-RNVO9AT

**Capture:** `2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (5,091 frames) | **Incident window:** 2024-09-04 (frame-relative t=0 to t≈3562s, ~59 min)

## 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **172.17.0.99** |
| MAC address | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** (Intel NIC vendor OUI) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** |
| Windows domain | BEPOSITIVE.COM (DC: WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19.bepositive.com at 172.17.0.17) |
| Logged-in user | **afletcher** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString, realm BEPOSITIVE.COM) |

Confirmed via DHCP Discover/Request (hostname option = DESKTOP-RNVO9AT, client MAC 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4), NBNS name registrations (DESKTOP-RNVO9AT<00>/<20>), and ARP (172.17.0.99 ↔ 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4).

## 2. Malware Family

**Koi Stealer** (Win32 information stealer). **Signature-confirmed** — Suricata/ET Pro rule fired directly on the traffic:

> `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` — 172.17.0.99 → 79.124.78.197:80 (48 hits)

This is corroborated behaviorally: repeated `POST /foots.php` requests to a hardcoded IP (no DNS lookup ever performed for it — the malware talks directly to the IP), `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` / `Content-Encoding: binary` bodies, a spoofed legacy IE7 User-Agent, and a steady-state ~40-byte encrypted body sent on a periodic beacon interval, consistent with a stealer checkin/heartbeat rather than legitimate web traffic. A companion ET rule also fired on the same flow (`ET INFO GENERIC SUSPICIOUS POST to Dotted Quad with Fake Browser`), reinforcing the classification.

A separate `GET/POST /index.php` exchange to the same host returned a plaintext gate token: `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|` — a task-ID/sub-ID/callback-URL descriptor typical of a pay-per-install loader gate, followed by an encrypted response blob (105 bytes). This indicates the same C2 infrastructure also serves a loader/task-delivery role in addition to stealer checkins. No malware binary/PE download was captured within this pcap, so no delivered-payload filename or SHA256 hash can be grounded in the traffic — the capture begins after initial compromise/execution.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in traffic)

**C2 endpoint:**
- `79.124.78.197:80/tcp` (HTTP, no reverse DNS/PTR queried by host — hardcoded IP)

**Malicious URLs (all on 79.124.78.197):**
- `POST http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` — Koi Stealer checkin (recurring, ~48 requests over the capture, body sizes 94/112/40 bytes settling to a steady 40-byte heartbeat)
- `GET http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` — loader gate request
- `POST http://79.124.78.197/index.php` — gate follow-up (105-byte encrypted request body)

**Malicious domains:** None — the malware C2 used a bare IPv4 address with no DNS resolution, avoiding domain-based detection.

**HTTP User-Agent used by the malware (spoofed):**
`Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0; .NET4.0C; .NET4.0E; .NET CLR 2.0.50727; .NET CLR 3.0.30729; .NET CLR 3.5.30729)`

**Transferred files / hashes:** None recoverable — all POST/response bodies on the C2 channel were encrypted/binary blobs (40–112 bytes); no executable, archive, or plaintext file was transferred in this capture, so no filename or SHA256 can be attributed.

**Not attributed to this incident (reviewed and ruled benign):** SMB/Kerberos alerts (`GPL NETBIOS SMB...`, `GPL RPC kerberos principal name overflow`) fired against 172.17.0.17, which is the host's own domain controller (WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19.bepositive.com) — this is normal AD/SMB traffic between the workstation and its DC, misfiring on generic legacy signatures, not exploitation. The `acroipm2.adobe.com` and Microsoft/MSN/Office TLS SNI traffic resolve to legitimate Akamai/Microsoft infrastructure and are background OS/application noise.

## Recommended Actions
- Isolate DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (172.17.0.99) from the network immediately.
- Block 79.124.78.197 at perimeter/firewall.
- Reset credentials for user **afletcher** (domain and local).
- Full disk/memory forensic acquisition of the host to recover the dropped Koi Stealer binary (not present in this pcap) and determine initial infection vector and any exfiltrated credential data.
